title: Snioland
subtitle: or, Iceland, Its Jokulls and Fjalls
summary: In June 1874 William Lord Watts sailed from Edinburgh to Iceland on the mail steamer “Diana”, on his second visit to the island. With a clergyman friend and Icelandic guides he travelled by pony and tent through the south: Reykjavick, Thingvellir, Geyser, Hecla, the Myrdals Jökull, and Katlugia. In August he went up Vatna Jökull from the south with three men and a hand-sleigh, planted a flag at what he took to be its centre, and turned back because of bad weather and short provisions; he returned to Reykjavick on 1 September. The book is written as a diary. An appendix gives advice and costs for visitors and notes on Iceland’s trade, volcanoes, history, and rocks, and a short list of its plants follows.

notes_on_text: The book has no chapters: it is a diary. The contents entries and the page divisions of the web and EPUB editions are the editor’s; their dates are those of the entries (the book dates one entry of early July “June 3rd”, kept as printed).
The numbered notes printed at the end of the book (pp. 181–182) are given there as in the book; their numerals in the text are not linked to them.

The book spells some Icelandic names with different accents in different places (Hvità and Hvitá, Thorsà and Thorsá, Oxera and Oxerà, Ströker and Strokër); each is given as printed. On p. 28 the second digit of the date “June 25th” is partly lost in the scan.
